name: ASML’s 0.33 NA NXE EUV platform
description: ASML’s NXE scanner generation introduced 0.33 numerical aperture for EUV wafer patterning and matured from development systems to tools suitable for volume production.

date.label: by 17 July 2013
date.basis: ASML’s 17 July release reports the shipment and installation process as underway.

events.statement: ASML was shipping and installing NXE:3300B scanners at customer sites.
events.caveats: This is a progress report on hardware introduction. Light-source development was underway.

evidence.locator: CEO statement and Second Quarter 2013 Product Highlights
evidence.supports: The results release describes the first NXE:3300B units in shipment and installation.

evidence.locator: Early NXE generations and We Are All In
evidence.supports: Yen identifies 0.33 NA on NXE:3300 and names TSMC as a 2013 receiver.

date.basis: Date or date granularity stated in the cited source.

events.statement: TSMC’s first NXE:3300 reached first light as part of its EUV process development.
events.place_note: Yen locates TSMC equipment development in Hsinchu, with related work in the Netherlands and US.

evidence.supports: The operator reports first light at the end of October and first-hand work on the same scanner.

date.basis: Date or date granularity stated in the cited source.

events.statement: ASML began shipping NXE:3400B, an upgraded NXE model aimed at production insertion.
events.caveats: A scanner shipment is distinct from a fab putting wafers into production.

evidence.locator: Slides 14–16, EUV highlights, production insertion and NXE:33x0B upgrade path
evidence.supports: The supplier identifies 2017 as the first shipment year and offers earlier-model upgrades.

date.basis: Date or date granularity stated in the cited source.

events.statement: ASML reached documented EUV tool readiness for high-volume manufacturing.
events.caveats: The cited tests are on equipment capability. Separate operator evidence establishes production on specific foundry processes.

evidence.supports: The engineers date readiness to 2018 and provide source and imaging performance evidence.

earliest_record.rationale: Contemporaneous manufacturer statements bound the start of 0.33 NA hardware delivery. First light at TSMC follows separately.

links.statement: The NXE development programme followed the Alpha Demo Tool work. TSMC reused its early EUV exposure experience in evaluating NXE:3100 before bringing in NXE:3300.
links.scope: Successive experimental and production-line scanners and customer learning, with NXE:3100 as an intermediate.

evidence.supports: A participating foundry lead describes the sequence and evaluates gains in optical performance at each step.

evidence.locator: The dawn of EUV, Toward industrialization, and First prototype to first light
evidence.supports: Supplier participant history traces Alpha Demo Tool trials to the late-2010 NXE:3100 and the 2013 NXE:3300 shipment.

links.caveats: The link covers the development path and experiments. The optical assemblies differ.
